name: create-next-agent-prompt
description: Create or refresh next_agent_prompt.md with an eligible implementation handoff or QA checkpoint status, on request or after a local Markdown ticket is fully completed.

# Create next-agent prompt

Write a self-contained implementation handoff using [implement-with-checkboxes](../implement-with-checkboxes/SKILL.md), or a QA handoff/waiting status when work reaches a human checkpoint. Save it to `next_agent_prompt.md` at the repository root unless the user specifies another destination. Creating the prompt does not start another implementation, QA session or harness run.

## Select the ticket

1. Read applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions and the repository's issue-tracker, readiness, and domain guidance. Inspect the worktree and any existing destination file; preserve unrelated changes. Use the feature and completed ticket supplied by the caller, or the user's explicit target. Ask for the feature only if repository context cannot identify it.
2. Read the approved spec/proposal, milestone membership/order and QA records, feature index, ticket headers, and needed completion evidence. Use the [shared planning reference](../references/planning.md#milestone-membership) for membership and approval boundaries and [ticket numbering](../references/planning.md#ticket-numbering) for ordering conventions. A readiness label alone is not prerequisite completion, and `Blocked by:` remains dependency history even after prerequisites finish. Verify completion from criterion evidence, checks, independent reviews, and implementation/bookkeeping commits rather than ticket numbers or header status alone. Missing or contradictory membership, order or acceptance evidence is a blocker to resolve, not permission to infer eligibility.
3. Identify the earliest required milestone whose human acceptance remains pending. Later milestones stay ineligible until the preceding required work is verified complete and its human acceptance is recorded for the assessed candidate. Within the eligible group, select open, unclaimed, agent-ready work with genuinely completed prerequisites in the approved preferred order. Honor explicit user selection and documented independent-experiment priorities within their eligibility rules. An older lower-numbered ticket cannot bypass plan order or QA gates. For an explicit but ineligible target, report its blockers instead of generating an executable assignment; do not silently substitute another feature or ticket.
4. When that group's required tickets are complete but its QA is pending, write the checkpoint handoff below, holding later required milestones. If remaining work has prerequisite/readiness blockers, write an explicit waiting status with evidence links. All tickets Done while final QA is unaccepted means **awaiting final QA**, not feature completion. Report feature completion only with verified required work and recorded final acceptance. Keep independent experiments' acceptance and priority separate as the approved plan defines them. Replace a stale generated execution prompt with the correct handoff/status.

## Gather focused context

For eligible implementation work, read the selected ticket, its referenced spec sections, relevant glossary/ADRs, current public contracts, documented checks, and prerequisite completion evidence. Inspect implementation entry points or existing tests only as needed to make the handoff concrete. Use the feature's context policy; do not replay sibling transcripts or load unrelated spec sections by default. At a checkpoint, gather the milestone QA context for the QA/status branch instead.

Identify every acceptance criterion, the public testing seam, compatibility requirements, explicit scope exclusions, and any unresolved decisions. Use the existing approved testing seam when one exists; otherwise tell the next agent to establish it with the user before writing tests. Preserve requirement wording and scope when translating criteria into implementation instructions.

For ownership and review context, apply the shared
[ownership and review-scope contract](../../../../docs/agents/ownership-review.md#repair-and-handoff).
Include the current approved owner/writer contract, affected unchanged flows and
changed/unchanged ownership explanation; direct both fresh reviewers to the shared
contract. Expose missing consequential decisions, omitted scope and pending work
with the next responsible action, using an explicit absence where none exists.

For review context, follow the [review record contract](../../../../docs/agents/review-records.md).
Carry assessment/report identities, current unresolved full finding keys, history,
human decision/amendment links and pending exact-source revalidation into the
handoff. Link original reports without rewriting them. A completed assessment or
risk disposition does not establish milestone acceptance or implementation eligibility.

For this repository's refactors 20–24 and their M1 checkpoint, carry the
[evaluated development-review guidance and corpus](../../../../docs/agents/reviewer-evaluation.md)
into either handoff branch. Name the evaluated version, original corpus/reports,
finite results and any unresolved limits. Keep new refactor reviews, cumulative
architecture assessment and human QA separate from the corpus evaluation.

Apply [development architecture checkpoints](../../../../docs/agents/architecture-checkpoints.md)
when selecting work and drafting either handoff branch. Carry start/post-change
trigger observations, required cumulative work, exact cumulative baseline/source,
inspected inventory and outstanding/deferred full finding keys. Missing/incomplete
or stale required assessment blocks affected integration/readiness; include the
next responsible action. When tickets are complete but cumulative work is absent,
write a preparation/waiting status, not a ready QA claim. A clean assessment can
progress autonomously within scope; actual candidate acceptance remains human-owned.

## Draft an implementation prompt

Write directly to the next agent, beginning with `Use $implement-with-checkboxes to implement only:` and the exact repository-relative ticket path. Include the ticket title, exact scoped spec references, and enough project-specific context to work without the preceding conversation. Use the current skills and tracker rules; keep detailed invariant workflows in their authoritative sources while making the consequential gates explicit in the handoff:

- **Starting state:** Follow `AGENTS.md`; capture the next agent's starting HEAD as its fixed review baseline; inspect/preserve the worktree; verify prerequisite implementation and completion evidence. Historical commit references are context, not a replacement for capturing that baseline.
- **Eligibility and role settings:** Name the approved plan and current milestone, selection evidence and next human boundary. Carry the agreed model, role guidance and context target using the [role and testing contracts](../references/planning.md#role-and-testing-contracts): worker and repair default to Medium with explicit ticket worker overrides applied to both; Spec and Standards default independently to High. Report missing model/configuration rather than guessing it. Require fresh assignments; a worker override does not change reviewer settings. Development settings do not claim runtime profile enforcement or skill capture.
- **Bounded implementation:** Cover every acceptance criterion with observable evidence, preserve existing passing/rejection behavior, document affected contracts, and name the deferred neighboring features. Do not expand the ticket or resolve an architectural decision the human still owns.
- **Environment and tests:** Read the repository's environment guidance before Python, dependency installation, or checks and use its reusable environment. Reference its testing policy and [test-strategy](../test-strategy/SKILL.md): map existing coverage before adding tests, select focused checks, and plan evidence capture during required verification. For executable behavior use `$tdd` at the agreed public seam, one failing behavioral test followed by its implementation per slice. Name the project's actual fixture/process/repository requirements and observable success/failure evidence. Preserve required complete-suite and explicit ticket checks. For standalone documentation/skill changes, carry the policy's document, link, routing and workflow validation; keep detailed check-selection and evidence-reuse rules in the testing policy.
- **Committed review:** After checks pass, commit only the implementation before `$code-review`, whose committed-diff review cannot see uncommitted work. Supply the captured baseline, ticket, and relevant spec requirements explicitly. Obtain separate fresh Spec and Standards reviews with their independent settings; fixture reviewers are not substitutes. For test changes, supply the coverage map, testing policy, and test-strategy's review guidance to these existing reviewers. Resolve blocking findings through fresh repair assignments with the worker setting, rerun affected required checks, commit repairs, and re-review the whole implementation against the original baseline. Record optional suggestions separately.
- **Completion bookkeeping:** After verified implementation and reviews, reconcile acceptance markers, set `**Status:** completed`, retain prior readiness in the completion comment, and preserve `Blocked by:`. Record implementation commits, criterion-specific evidence, actual checks, independent review outcomes, and unresolved items; link evidence from the feature index. Commit only this ticket's bookkeeping separately from implementation. If verification fails, leave unverified criteria unchecked and report the exact blocker.
- **Next handoff:** After implementation and bookkeeping are committed and fully complete, follow the implementation skill's automatic `$create-next-agent-prompt` step, including its separate handoff commit and final report. Select through milestone eligibility again; at a human boundary create a QA handoff/waiting status. Ticket completion and plan approval do not accept milestones or complete the feature before final QA.
- **Boundaries and report:** Keep each agent within the applicable context target (250K active context for this feature unless changed by the user). Preserve approved inputs belonging to an active harness run and report that condition as a blocker to mutations. Do not push without explicit authorization. Report implementation/bookkeeping commits, check and review outcomes, unchecked criteria, and the next prompt path or exact handoff blocker. Claim completion only when the required gates actually passed.

Adapt these instructions to the selected ticket rather than copying the previous ticket's criteria, exclusions, expected results, or test counts. Link prerequisite evidence instead of treating old outcomes as proof of the new implementation.

## Draft a QA handoff or waiting status

Begin with the actual status, such as **Awaiting milestone QA**, **Awaiting final QA**, or **Waiting: prerequisite evidence missing**. Identify the approved plan/version, milestone and membership, verified completion evidence, pending acceptance/blockers and which later work remains ineligible. Use the milestone's planned human checks, setup, expected observations and acceptance conditions; distinguish development checkpoints from target-repository runtime QA in fixtures.

Carry outstanding review work and the inspected/omitted scope using the shared
[ownership and review-scope contract](../../../../docs/agents/ownership-review.md#repair-and-handoff),
including unresolved full finding keys, missing reports, pending revalidation and
human decisions or their explicit absence. Keep the next responsible action
visible without treating review completion as QA acceptance.

Carry exact existing QA request and artifact paths/identities, run identity, feature revision, development base, tested candidate revision, gate evidence, decision location and recorded decision when available. Label missing references explicitly; a plan without runtime artifacts receives a preparation/waiting status with the missing inputs and next responsible workflow, not invented request IDs, candidates, results or acceptance. Identify a known stale/mismatched decision as pending renewed assessment. Link actual records without authoring or altering an approval artifact.

Keep candidate preparation, promotion, continuation, QA-session execution and approval authority with their separately authorized workflows. State the next human/workflow action without launching it. An implementation or repair worker cannot accept a candidate. Only recorded human acceptance of the assessed inputs can satisfy the checkpoint; changed inputs require renewed acceptance under the approved contract.

## Save and verify

Write the actual prompt as Markdown, without an enclosing code fence or unresolved template placeholders. Refresh an existing generated handoff; preserve unrelated user-authored content or edits, using a separate destination and reporting the conflict if they cannot be retained safely.

Read the saved file back. Check every ticket/spec/evidence path, criterion coverage, milestone/prerequisite eligibility, role settings, scope boundaries, and consistency with the current implementation skill. For QA/status outputs check that known request/candidate/artifact identities are exact, missing inputs remain explicit, and no approval is inferred. An ineligible or QA-pending handoff must clearly identify its status, without instructing the next milestone to execute.

Return the destination, selected ticket and selection reason, or the checkpoint/blocker/verified-complete status. When invoked by `implement-with-checkboxes`, leave committing the generated handoff to that caller; when invoked directly, commit only if requested. Never launch the next agent as part of this skill.

# Implement with checkboxes

Read and follow [Matt's implementation skill](../../matt-pocock/implement/SKILL.md) for the assigned ticket. This wrapper adds the review checkpoint, completion bookkeeping, and next-agent handoff below; keep the upstream skill unchanged. Where a Skill tool is unavailable, read the referenced skill and perform its workflow directly.

Read the [shared planning reference](../references/planning.md#milestone-membership) for milestone membership and approval boundaries, and its [role and testing contracts](../references/planning.md#role-and-testing-contracts) for defaults and overrides. Use the approved plan's earliest eligible milestone and preferred order, verified prerequisites, and recorded human QA decisions to confirm the assignment is eligible. An explicit target or older lower ticket number cannot bypass a human checkpoint; report the exact blocker for an ineligible assignment.

Use fresh implementation and repair assignments with Medium reasoning by default; apply an explicit ticket worker override to both. Configure the separate fresh Spec and Standards assignments independently, each defaulting to High. Carry the approved model, role guidance and context target; report missing configuration rather than inventing it. These are development assignment settings, not proof of runtime profile enforcement or skill capture.

Read and apply the shared [ownership and review-scope contract](../../../../docs/agents/ownership-review.md)
before implementation/repair and when preparing both upstream `code-review`
assignments. Record the affected flow and changed/unchanged ownership in the
implementation evidence; supply the shared contract to each fresh reviewer. Its
whole-ticket scope and report requirements take precedence over upstream
diff-hunk-only wording and the under-400-word report briefs; retain a concise
summary with enough linked detail for the required evidence.

For this repository's ownership refactors 20–24, use the
[evaluated development-review guidance and corpus](../../../../docs/agents/reviewer-evaluation.md)
when preparing both fresh review assignments. Carry the evaluated guidance
identity and finite limitations; corpus reports do not review the new refactor.

Apply [development architecture checkpoints](../../../../docs/agents/architecture-checkpoints.md)
at ticket start and after implementation. Record each risk trigger and required
broader assessment before integration; no-trigger tickets retain the two existing
review axes. At milestone readiness, carry the cumulative assessment, exact source,
prior findings and missing/stale work into the handoff; a completed review alone
never accepts a milestone.

## Implement and review

Read the repo-owned [review record contract](../../../../docs/agents/review-records.md)
when preparing assessments, saving reports or handling findings. Use its templates
to attach routine Spec/Standards reports to one ticket assessment, preserve the
original baseline/reports and carry full finding keys/history into repairs and
independent re-review. Keep assessment completion, outstanding findings and human
QA separate; record human-owned decisions rather than inferring authority.

1. Follow `AGENTS.md` and the ticket's scoped spec references. Read the repository's [issue-tracker conventions](../../../../docs/agents/issue-tracker.md) and [testing policy](../../../../docs/agents/testing.md). Capture the starting `HEAD` as the review baseline and inspect the worktree, preserving unrelated changes. When adding or changing tests, use [test-strategy](../test-strategy/SKILL.md) to map existing coverage and choose verification scope before the upstream TDD workflow. Implement only the assigned ticket. Use the testing policy's focused development checks and required completion checks; standalone documentation/skill work receives its documented validation rather than an artificial TDD cycle or runtime suite replay.
2. After checks pass, create a checkpoint commit containing only this implementation **before** invoking `code-review`: its current committed-diff review cannot see uncommitted changes. Supply the captured baseline, ticket, and relevant spec requirements. For later repairs, keep that original baseline so the review covers the whole implementation.
3. Obtain the upstream skill's separate, fresh Spec and Standards reviews with the independently configured reviewer settings above. For test changes, supply the coverage map, testing policy, and test-strategy's review guidance to these existing reviewers. Scripted fixture reviewers verify harness behavior; they do not replace reviews of the implementation itself. Resolve blocking findings through fresh repair assignments with the worker setting, rerun affected required checks, commit fixes, and re-review the whole implementation against the original baseline. Record optional suggestions without treating them as mandatory fixes. If implementation already exists and the diff is empty, verify its recorded checks and reviews against the current revision instead of treating an empty review as a pass.

## Reconcile the ticket

After implementation checks and reviews, apply the tracker's **Completion bookkeeping** rules. Map each acceptance criterion to evidence from the verified implementation revision; completing code or receiving an agent's success report alone is insufficient.

Update satisfied acceptance checkboxes. Once every criterion and required gate is verified, set the ticket's header to `**Status:** completed`; record its previous readiness label in the completion comment. Keep `Blocked by:` as the declared dependency history. If verification is incomplete, retain the existing readiness status and explain what remains pending.

Append the completion comment and link evidence from the feature index when present. Before committing, verify that the acceptance markers, header status, completion comment, and feature index agree on the verified outcome. Commit these documentation changes separately from the reviewed implementation; stage only this ticket's bookkeeping. Review any subsequent code changes through the implementation gates again.

Declare the ticket complete only when every criterion is verified, required checks pass, blocking findings are resolved, and implementation and bookkeeping are committed. If a required step fails or approved inputs belong to an active harness run, report the exact blocker and leave completion pending.

## Create the next-agent handoff

After the ticket is fully completed and its implementation and bookkeeping commits exist, automatically call `$create-next-agent-prompt` using [its skill instructions](../create-next-agent-prompt/SKILL.md). Supply the completed ticket, approved plan/milestones, feature index, completion evidence, role settings, recorded QA references and any explicit user sequencing preferences. Where a Skill tool is unavailable, read that skill and perform its workflow directly. It selects eligible implementation work or writes a QA handoff/waiting status at a checkpoint. Ticket completion does not accept a milestone; all tickets Done while final QA is unaccepted does not complete the feature. This step creates the handoff without starting another ticket.

Commit the generated `next_agent_prompt.md` (or the user's chosen destination) separately from implementation and ticket bookkeeping, staging only the generated handoff. If no ticket is eligible, save and commit the skill's handoff status instead of leaving a stale execution prompt. If prompt creation or its commit is blocked, report the completed ticket and the exact handoff blocker without claiming the handoff is ready.

Report the implementation, bookkeeping, and handoff commit references, checks, independent review outcomes, any unchecked criteria, and the next prompt path with its selected ticket or checkpoint/blocker status. Keep orchestration, candidate preparation/promotion, QA-session execution and approval recording in their separately authorized workflows. This development wrapper neither supplies human acceptance nor launches runtime work.

# Shared planning reference

This is the authoritative planning policy for custom planning workflows and
their generated bundles. Upstream skills supply interview, domain, synthesis,
and slicing procedures; this reference augments their outputs and governs when
publication is allowed. It defines planning documents, not a runtime schema.

## Context and draft boundary

Read the target repository's `AGENTS.md`, domain glossary and relevant ADRs,
tracker and triage conventions, testing policy, and existing feature inputs.
Use project requirements and accepted architecture decisions over general design
heuristics. Reuse existing custom guidance before proposing another policy.
Resolve environment facts by inspection; decisions belong to the human.

For consequential mutable state, apply the repo-owned
[ownership and review-scope contract](../../../../docs/agents/ownership-review.md#planning-and-implementation)
when grilling decisions and drafting implementation contracts. Carry the owner,
permitted writers, invariant-preserving operations, persistence/restoration and
failure rules into the spec; resolve consequential gaps before approval.

For this repository, read [domain guidance](../../../../docs/agents/domain.md),
[tracker conventions](../../../../docs/agents/issue-tracker.md),
[triage vocabulary](../../../../docs/agents/triage-labels.md), and
[testing policy](../../../../docs/agents/testing.md) before the corresponding work.
For another target, use that project's equivalents; ask only for missing
decisions that cannot be inferred from its guidance or the conversation.

For this repository's ownership refactors 20–24, carry the
[evaluated development-review guidance and corpus](../../../../docs/agents/reviewer-evaluation.md)
into the implementation/review context. Preserve its exact guidance identity,
finite observations and unresolved limits; later refactor evidence and M1 QA
remain separate required work.

Keep proposals in the conversation or an explicitly marked draft location,
separate from published inputs. A suitable local staging location is
`.scratch/<feature>/drafts/<version>/`; mark each document **Draft — unapproved**.
Before approval, keep proposed individual ticket bodies inside `ticket-proposal.md`
rather than publishing files under `issues/`. Existing approved spec, tickets,
milestones and index stay unchanged. Proposed glossary/ADR changes affecting an
approved contract belong with the draft until accepted; ordinary resolved domain
terms can be captured using the project's domain-modeling procedure.

For an existing plan, identify the approved version and its immutable inputs.
Draft the proposed version separately, with an explicit change summary and
unchanged requirements carried forward. Preserve completed-ticket identities,
historical evidence, and prior versions. Active-run inputs stay immutable;
approval of a revision permits a separate new version, not an in-place edit of
the active version. External publication requires its own authorization.

## Grilling decisions and shared understanding

Use grilling's frontier rounds: ask only decisions whose prerequisites are
settled, give recommendations, and wait for answers. Use domain modeling to
resolve overloaded terms and test domain relationships with concrete scenarios.
Consult [deep-module guidance](../../matt-pocock/codebase-design/SKILL.md) when
interfaces or ownership need design work. Record these decisions:

- User problem, intended outcomes, actors, scope, and explicit exclusions.
- Important interfaces, ownership of invariants, external dependencies, and
  observable failure behavior. Leave internal implementation choices to workers.
- Agreed behavioral testing seams, existing prior art, required check commands
  or named gates, and evidence needed to establish success. Prefer existing
  public seams; explicitly agree any new seam with the human using
  [test strategy](../test-strategy/SKILL.md).
- Required work versus independent experiments or optional follow-ups; genuine
  prerequisite edges; ticket size and any prefactoring necessary for green slices.
- Meaningful earlier capabilities for human QA, plus final acceptance; or the
  user's every-N-ticket cadence. Set explicit membership, concrete human checks,
  observable pass conditions, and how earlier gates constrain later work.
- Worker/repair and separate Spec/Standards settings, ticket overrides, and
  applicable role guidance. Resolve ambiguous settings before approval.

Summarize settled decisions, proposed scope, testing seams, defaults and QA
strategy. The frontier must be empty for the proposed scope, and the user must
confirm shared understanding before synthesis. Confirmation authorizes drafting;
it is distinct from approval to publish the eventual bundle.

## Synthesis and joint revision

Use to-spec's problem/solution/stories/decisions/testing structure and to-tickets'
vertical slices and blocking edges. Each ticket delivers an independently
verifiable outcome small enough for one fresh context. Mechanical wide refactors
use upstream expand–migrate–contract guidance when vertical slicing cannot land
green. Specify contracts rather than prescribing internal classes or file layouts.

Present the spec and ticket/milestone proposal as one draft version. Include each
proposed ticket's complete body, not only its title; the user must be able to
approve the acceptance criteria, dependencies and exceptions before publication.
Ask whether granularity and blocking edges are correct, which slices need merging
or splitting, and whether the QA actions demonstrate the intended capabilities.

Apply feedback to the spec and proposal together. A changed outcome must update
the spec, affected ticket criteria/dependencies, milestone membership/QA, and any
testing or role settings it changes. Record the changes so the next approval
identifies the revised bundle. Pure clarification can be edited directly;
consequential new scope, interface, invariant, testing seam, dependency, or QA
decisions reopen only the affected grilling frontier and its dependent questions.
Confirm the resulting shared understanding before synthesizing the new version.

## Milestone membership

Always include a final milestone covering completion of every required ticket
and overall feature acceptance. Its required membership can be only the final
group; explicitly state cumulative coverage of earlier accepted groups. A single
milestone is reasonable for a small feature, but still propose earlier meaningful
capability checkpoints and explain when no useful earlier boundary exists.

By default group tickets into demonstrable capabilities. For an explicit every-N
request, fix a topological ticket order using genuine dependencies and agreed
priority, then partition it into groups of N with a smaller final group when
needed. For example seven tickets at N=3 produce groups 01–03, 04–06, and 07.
Record the actual IDs, not a dynamic rule such as "whichever three finish next".
If a requested order conflicts with dependencies, propose a valid order or ask
the human to resolve the conflict; do not quietly change N or invent edges.

Assign every required ticket to exactly one required milestone. Dependencies may
point within its group or to an earlier group, never a later group. Milestone IDs
remain stable across accepted versions; record any approved membership change.
An independent experiment can have a separate selection and final acceptance;
declare its priority without making it a release prerequisite accidentally.

For each milestone give QA setup, actions the human can perform, expected
observable results, and acceptance evidence. Distinguish ticket Done, milestone
accepted/promoted, and feature complete. Later groups wait for human acceptance
of the previous group; all tickets Done still requires final QA. Plan approval
does not accept a candidate. Actual request identities, candidates, decisions,
execution, promotion and continuation are owned by later runtime/QA workflows.

Before required milestone QA readiness, apply
[development architecture checkpoints](../../../../docs/agents/architecture-checkpoints.md).
Plan cumulative work with the prior accepted milestone or feature starting revision,
complete workflow inventory and carried findings. Assess lifecycle, restoration,
shared-state and writer risks at ticket start and after implementation; triggered
work requires broader assessment before integration. Keep review completion,
finding dispositions, candidate readiness and human acceptance separate.

## Ticket numbering

By default, number a new local ticket bundle consecutively in its preferred
execution order, with blockers before dependents and required milestones in
their planned order. Start at 01 for a fresh feature; continue after any existing
IDs when adding tickets. Within a milestone, use agreed priority to order
independent tickets. Numbering expresses a readable preferred sequence; retain
genuine dependency edges so independent work can still run in parallel.

Place an independent experiment at its intended scheduling point in that
sequence while keeping its separate membership and acceptance. For example,
if an experiment follows the backend slice, give it the next number before
later release work; numbering alone must not make it a release prerequisite.
Human QA gates still determine when later milestones become eligible.

Settle the draft order before assigning final IDs. When feedback reorders,
splits or adds draft tickets, refresh their numbers, filenames, dependency
links, milestone membership, proposal and index together before approval.
Present the numbered proposal in ascending order so the human can inspect
the intended sequence without a separate reordering request.

For revisions, preserve already published IDs, completed-ticket evidence and
captured run inputs. If preserving published IDs prevents sequential order,
show the exception explicitly. Renumber published open tickets only when the
human requests it; retain an old-to-new mapping and update live references
without rewriting historical identities or active-run inputs.

## Role and testing contracts

Record these defaults in the bundle unless the human chooses explicit alternatives:

| Role | Reasoning | Configuration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Implementation and repair | Medium | One worker setting; a ticket worker override applies to both roles. |
| Spec reviewer | High | Independently configured from worker and Standards. |
| Standards reviewer | High | Independently configured from worker and Spec. |

Record the agreed model for each role; do not silently guess model availability.
Use fresh assignments, and record any agreed active-context target. For each
ticket, state its worker override and reason or explicitly inherit the default.
A worker override never changes reviewer settings. Record local source references
for required guidance, project defaults by role, and ticket additions by role.
Additions supplement defaults and preserve required role/output/access contracts.
Unselected installed skills are not automatically run inputs. Runtime skill
resolution/capture and model-profile execution remain separate work.

Preserve agreed interfaces, invariants and testing seams in the spec, with each
ticket linking its relevant contracts and checks. State behavioral coverage and
required gates without duplicating implementation details. QA actions complement
automated gates; neither replaces the other. A new testing seam or changed check
requirement is a planning decision, not an internal worker convenience.

## Complete bundle shape

For the local Markdown tracker, publish the following under `.scratch/<feature>/`
(or the target's configured versioned destination). Use actual values throughout;
the fields below are a checklist, not executable metadata. Link relative paths
and section anchors so a fresh worker can find the approved contracts.

### `spec.md`

- Title, plan version, approval record/reference, and relationship to any prior version.
- **Problem Statement**, **Solution**, and numbered **User Stories** covering the
  agreed behavior, failures and actors.
- **Implementation Decisions**: agreed interfaces, invariants, ownership and
  constraints; applicable domain/design references; deferred internal choices.
- **Testing Decisions**: agreed seams, prior art, behavioral coverage, required
  commands or named gate references, and expected evidence.
- **Role Configuration**: model/reasoning defaults for worker/repair, Spec and
  Standards independently; context targets and required/default guidance sources.
- **Milestone Contract**: link to explicit membership, QA and final coverage.
- **Out of Scope** and **Further Notes**, including unresolved matters if still
  a draft. Required decisions must be resolved before approval/publication.

### `ticket-proposal.md`

- Draft/approved state and version matching the spec; summary of changes from
  the prior proposal and any approved version.
- Each ticket's full proposed body using the individual-ticket shape below.
- Dependency graph or edge list, preferred topological order, milestone table
  with actual ticket IDs, and the role/testing exceptions being proposed.
- Questions/feedback and their resolution; approval scope and decision reference
  once accepted. After publication link the individual ticket files.

### `issues/<NN>-<slug>.md` (one per approved ticket)

```markdown
# <NN>: <Outcome title>

**What to build:** <complete bounded end-to-end behavior>
**Blocked by:** <numbers, titles and links, or None (can start immediately)>
**Status:** <target triage label; ready-for-agent only when sufficiently specified>
**Plan version:** <approved version; link to spec>
**Milestone:** <stable ID; link to membership and QA>
**Worker reasoning:** <inherit Medium, or explicit override and rationale; applies to repair>
**Role guidance:** <inherit project defaults; additions by role with local source references>
**Context:** <scoped spec contracts, domain/design references, agreed seam and check references>

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] <observable requirement and evidence that verifies it>
- [ ] <failure/constraint requirement where applicable>

## Verification

<agreed behavioral seam, required checks and evidence; link shared requirements>
```

Apply [ticket numbering](#ticket-numbering). Readiness is separate from satisfied
dependencies or execution state. New acceptance markers remain unchecked. Include
a model/context override here if agreed; absent overrides inherit the spec defaults.

### `milestones.md`

- Version and approval reference, stable ordered IDs, named capabilities, fixed
  required ticket membership and gate into each next group.
- For each group: QA setup/actions, expected results and observable acceptance
  conditions, required evidence, and initial state **not yet requested/accepted**.
- Final checkpoint identified explicitly, with cumulative coverage of all
  required work and overall feature acceptance.
- Separate optional/experiment membership and priority where applicable.

### `README.md` (feature index)

- Version, approval scope/reference, links to spec, proposal and milestones.
- Every ticket's ID/title/link, declared dependencies, readiness and milestone;
  preferred execution order and current eligible group without claiming execution.
- Final QA requirement and distinction between plan approval and QA acceptance.
- Link prior versions/change summary for revisions; preserve existing completion
  evidence. A published plan alone does not claim any ticket or milestone complete.

## Approval, validation and publication

Before requesting publication approval, show the complete current spec and
proposal, including the ticket bodies, milestone definitions, defaults/overrides
and testing contracts. Identify version and intended destination. Explain that
the decision covers the coherent bundle; approval of scope, one ticket, or shared
understanding alone does not approve publication of unseen material.

Use an explicit human approval that identifies this current bundle. Existing
authorization suffices when it clearly covers the material being published;
do not ask again merely because a stage changed. If approval is declined,
withheld, ambiguous, or only partial, retain the draft and report the unresolved
scope. No individual tickets, canonical spec, milestones or index are published
until coherent-bundle approval is established. Silence is not approval.

Validate the approved draft before publication:

- Every agreed outcome maps to spec behavior and verifiable ticket criteria;
  spec/proposal/ticket defaults, overrides, testing contracts and QA agree.
- IDs and dependencies exist and are unique; graph is acyclic, and declared
  external prerequisites have explicit completion requirements.
- New ticket numbers follow the preferred execution sequence and milestone
  order, with blockers before dependents and experiments at their agreed
  scheduling points. Any preserved-ID exception is explicit; proposal order,
  filenames, headings, dependency links, milestones and index agree.
- Every required ticket has exactly one membership, dependencies respect group
  ordering, cadence matches the request, and final cumulative coverage is complete.
- Every milestone has actionable QA and acceptance conditions; no contradictory
  settings, unresolved required decisions, or fabricated acceptance remain.
- References resolve, ticket bodies match those approved, and the destination
  preserves existing approved inputs and unrelated work.

If validation requires a substantive change, revise the draft and obtain approval
for that changed scope. Publish all files of the validated bundle, then check
their cross-links, version, membership and criteria agree and record the human's
approval reference without inventing a decision or timestamp. Report paths and
any remaining execution prerequisites. This workflow authors approved inputs;
it does not implement scheduling, branch promotion, approval watching, restart,
QA execution, background launch, or runtime skill selection. Generated-bundle
runtime and skill-metadata proof remains ticket 37 in the harness project.

"""Audit retained identities, routing, links and preservation; never score judgment."""
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import unquote
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import re
import runpy
import subprocess

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
EV = ROOT / '.scratch/ticket-harness/evidence'
CASE = EV / '19-evaluation'
BASE = 'f2929e79cfd5a68f670862775053ae85ba9582b5'
DOCS = ['docs/agents/reviewer-evaluation.md',
        '.agents/skills/custom/references/planning.md',
        '.agents/skills/custom/implement-with-checkboxes/SKILL.md',
        '.agents/skills/custom/create-next-agent-prompt/SKILL.md']

def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()

def git(*args):
    return subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(ROOT), *args], text=True).strip()

def main():
    changed = set(git('diff', '--name-only', BASE).splitlines() + git('ls-files', '--others', '--exclude-standard').splitlines())
    for name in changed:
        assert name in DOCS or name.startswith('.scratch/ticket-harness/evidence/19-'), name
    protected = set(git('ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only', BASE).splitlines()) - set(DOCS)
    assert not protected & changed, sorted(protected & changed)
    for commit in ['4814eabd4bf2f196f7fb6915667c4305b7c2d0b9', '91e285ff3cb1b46f4404b7fc534625637bdff015', '816aecbaa67f79ca5fd97c78f40593cdb007c45a', 'aef9625c3d155815df22f3e827559ef23fcdcf03']:
        subprocess.run(['git', 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', commit, BASE], cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    manifest = json.loads((CASE/'source-manifest.json').read_text())
    identity = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(manifest, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
    assert identity == (CASE/'corpus-identity.txt').read_text().strip()
    assert set(manifest) == {str(p.relative_to(CASE/'snapshot')) for p in (CASE/'snapshot').rglob('*') if p.is_file()}
    temp = Path('/tmp/development-review-19-g1')
    for name, digest in manifest.items():
        assert sha(CASE/'snapshot'/name) == digest, name
        assert sha(temp/name) == digest, ('supplied snapshot changed', name)
        assert (temp/name).stat().st_mode & 0o222 == 0, name
        if name.startswith('guidance/'):
            # Routing docs added by this ticket are not substantive G1 reviewer instructions.
            original = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', BASE+':'+name.removeprefix('guidance/')], cwd=ROOT)
            assert original == (CASE/'snapshot'/name).read_bytes(), name
    declaration = json.loads((CASE/'declaration-capture.json').read_text())
    assert sha(CASE/'declaration.md') == declaration['declaration_sha256']
    assert sha(CASE/'source-manifest.json') == declaration['source_manifest_sha256']
    assignments = json.loads((CASE/'assignments.json').read_text())['assignments']
    assert len(assignments) == 2
    declared_at = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(declaration['declared_at_utc'])
    for row in assignments:
        assert declared_at < datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(row['timestamp'].replace('Z','+00:00'))
        assert row['settings'] == {'fork_turns':'none', 'model':'gpt-6.1-sol', 'reasoning_effort':'high'}
        assert sha(CASE/row['prompt_path']) == row['prompt_sha256']
        # Serialized dispatch messages are opaque; the recipient preserves readable input.
        prompt = (CASE/(row['label']+'-input.txt')).read_text()
        assert str(temp) in prompt and identity in prompt
    captured = json.loads((CASE/'review-capture.json').read_text())
    for name, digest in captured['sha256'].items():
        assert sha(CASE/name) == digest, name
    supplement = json.loads((CASE/'review-capture-supplement.json').read_text())
    for row in supplement['axes'].values():
        assert sha(CASE/row['source_records_path']) == row['source_records_sha256']
        assert row['custom_tool_call_count'] == row['custom_tool_output_count'] > 0
    anchors = runpy.run_path(str(EV/'16-check.py'))['anchors']
    docs = [ROOT/name for name in DOCS] + [EV/'19-implementation-report.md'] + list(CASE.glob('*.md'))
    links = []
    for path in docs:
        text = re.sub(r'^```[^\n]*\n.*?^```\s*$', '', path.read_text(), flags=re.M|re.S)
        text = re.sub(r'`[^`\n]+`', '', text)
        for href in re.findall(r'\[[^\]]*\]\(([^\s)]+)\)', text):
            if re.match(r'[a-z]+://', href):
                continue
            name, _, fragment = unquote(href).partition('#')
            name = re.sub(r':\d+$', '', name)
            target = (path.parent/name).resolve() if name else path
            assert target.exists(), (path, href)
            if fragment:
                assert fragment in anchors(target), (path, href)
            links.append({'from':str(path.relative_to(ROOT)), 'href':href})
    for name in DOCS[1:]:
        assert 'reviewer-evaluation.md' in (ROOT/name).read_text(), name
    # The retained guidance deliberately has unsupplied outgoing context pointers.
    # REVIEW.md bounds their resolution; never pull key-bearing specs into reviewer input.
    assert not list((CASE/'snapshot').rglob('*declaration*'))
    assert not (CASE/'snapshot/guidance/.scratch').exists()
    result = {'result':'pass', 'recorded_at_utc':datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
              'baseline':BASE, 'head_before_checkpoint':git('rev-parse','HEAD'),
              'scope':'standalone documentation/skill evidence; no runtime tests or judgment scoring',
              'source_identities':{str(p.relative_to(ROOT)):sha(p) for p in docs if not p.name.endswith('-raw.md')},
              'helpers':{str(p.relative_to(ROOT)):sha(p) for p in [Path(__file__),EV/'19-run-checks.sh',CASE/'build_corpus.py',CASE/'capture_reviews.py']},
              'retained_evidence_identities':{str(p.relative_to(ROOT)):sha(p) for p in sorted(CASE.rglob('*')) if p.is_file()},
              'corpus_identity':identity, 'corpus_files':len(manifest),
              'protected_baseline_paths':len(protected), 'local_links':links,
              'review_capture':captured, 'assignments':assignments,
              'limits':'Link/hash/routing audits do not establish reviewer judgment. See manual per-case adjudication and original reports.'}
    stamp = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ')
    target = EV/f'19-check-results-{stamp}.json'
    target.write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')
    print(json.dumps({'result':'pass','source_manifest':identity,'corpus_files':len(manifest),'protected_paths':len(protected),'local_links':len(links),'result_path':str(target.relative_to(ROOT))},indent=2))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

class Attempt:
    def __init__(self, identity):
        self._record = {"id": deepcopy(identity), "status": "running", "revision": None}
        self._current = deepcopy(self._record)

    def submit(self, revision):
        if self._record["status"] != "running" or not revision:
            raise ValueError("invalid submission")
        self._transition("submitted", revision)

    def complete(self):
        if self._record["status"] != "submitted":
            raise ValueError("invalid completion")
        self._transition("completed", self._record["revision"])

    def _transition(self, status, revision):
        updated = deepcopy({**self._record, "status": status, "revision": revision})
        current = deepcopy(updated)
        self._record = updated
        self._current = current

    def snapshot(self):
        return deepcopy(self._record), deepcopy(self._current)
''')

# Saved checks
Run owns durable gates and verified references. `record` registers successful evidence;
`save` and `restore` preserve JSON keys and later source invalidation semantics.
Verified references resolve to the same canonical gate records used by durable
reporting, so changing a source marks both views invalid. QA reads the verified
view. The caller may invalidate source A after restoring a deliberate stop.
Only Run writes these records; consumer functions are read-only. No concurrency.

# Repository preflight
`validate` owns the local repository preflight and returns the resolved root and
requested branch. Reject failed Git commands, detached HEAD, an unexpected branch,
a dirty worktree (including untracked files), absent base revision, and a base that
is not an ancestor of HEAD. Read-only; no saved state or mutation. The injected
`git` callable accepts argument lists and returns CompletedProcess-like results;
it runs against the requested checkout with text capture, never a shell. Git
failure details may be reduced to ValueError. No class requirement or generic
validation framework. The caller selects policies through `expected_branch` and
`base`; it should not reproduce these validation decisions.

# Report handoff
An attempt's validated human-decision handoff belongs to that attempt even after
a later attempt starts. History preserves all attempts in start order. Report
work may finish after another attempt has been appended. `attach` receives the
attempt ID supplied by the report command; validation ensures handoff content
is valid for that ID. Checking validates and returns report information; it
must not choose or edit an attempt from shared history. Execution locates the
identified owner and asks it to attach the handoff. Consumers read by attempt ID.
Unknown IDs reject without changing any attempt. No durable checkpoint here.

# Plan parsing
`parse` returns a fresh tuple of frozen Ticket values from comma-separated
`id:dependency+dependency` entries, rejecting missing/duplicate IDs, missing
referenced dependencies and cycles. IDs are trimmed nonempty strings; empty
right sides mean no dependencies. Output preserves declaration order and each
dependency's order. No external resources, lifecycle, mutable shared data or
persistence. Configuration contains only this syntax. Readiness calculations
consume the immutable result. Keep ordinary transformations as functions.

# Submission observations
Attempt owns submission and the mirrored current-ticket observation. Both normal
worker and repair entry paths preserve the same transition invariant: only a
running attempt may submit, its revision and status change together, and the
current-ticket fields reflect that attempt. Changes to submission policy must
have one owning operation; entry callers delegate rather than reproduce record
edits. State is in-memory and deliberately exposes records to read-only reporting.
Only the owner may write those records. No concurrent calls or persistence here.

def receive_repair(attempt, revision):
    if attempt.record["status"] != "running":
        raise ValueError("not running")
    attempt.record["revision"] = revision
    attempt.record["status"] = "submitted"
    attempt.ticket["attempt"] = attempt.record["id"]
    attempt.ticket["revision"] = revision
    attempt.ticket["status"] = "submitted"

def receive_worker(attempt, revision):
    attempt.submit(revision)

# Local IO
`atomic_write` replaces a local UTF-8 file with complete text using a temporary
file on the same filesystem. Existing content survives an exception before replace;
temporary files are cleaned on failure. Caller supplies a directory that exists.
No crash durability/fsync or metadata preservation guarantee. `invoke` runs an
argument vector without a shell, in a supplied cwd with text capture and finite
timeout, returning nonzero exits for the caller's domain policy; TimeoutExpired
propagates. These primitives own no run/attempt/review state and perform no domain
record mutations. No persistence beyond the explicitly written file.

import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile

def atomic_write(destination, text):
    destination = Path(destination)
    temporary = None
    try:
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", encoding="utf-8",
                                         dir=destination.parent, delete=False) as file:
            temporary = Path(file.name)
            file.write(text)
        os.replace(temporary, destination)
    finally:
        if temporary is not None:
            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)

def invoke(argv, cwd, timeout):
    return subprocess.run(argv, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True,
                          timeout=timeout, check=False)

# Prepared input
Preparation owns configuration validation and normalization. Both CLI and resumed
entry paths must return a complete Prepared result: nonempty selected IDs,
normalized unique membership preserving first order, and a positive repair limit
(default 2). Raw configuration is copied, never mutated. Callers may consume the
prepared result directly; they must not finish its initialization in a particular
order or know derived-field rules. Invalid repair limit rejects during preparation,
not later during execution. Result state is in-memory, no checkpoint serialization.

from preparation import prepare

def from_cli(raw):
    prepared = prepare(raw)
    prepared.selected = tuple(dict.fromkeys(raw["selected"]))
    prepared.repair_limit = int(raw.get("repair_limit", 2))
    if prepared.repair_limit < 1:
        raise ValueError("invalid repair limit")
    return prepared

# Attempt operations
Attempt owns running -> submitted -> completed transitions and mirrored current
observations. Construction sets both views consistently. Submission requires a
running attempt and nonempty revision; completion requires a submitted attempt.
Invalid operations leave both views untouched. Consumers receive copied snapshots;
caller-owned input dictionaries cannot mutate state. No persistence or concurrency.
Caller asks for operations; it does not edit the record. A small class is permitted
because these operations own a real invariant. No general state-machine framework.

# Test strategy

Manage the value and cost of regression coverage. [TDD](../../matt-pocock/tdd/SKILL.md) owns the red/green loop;
this skill owns which behaviors need tests, which existing tests suffice, and
which checks to run. Read the repository's testing policy and required checks
before choosing verification scope. Follow applicable glossary and ADR guidance.

## During implementation

Before adding tests, inspect the existing coverage at the approved seams. Make a
brief map from each changed requirement or failure mode to an existing test, an
extension, or a missing case. Keep this map in the current task notes or completion
evidence; a separate document is usually unnecessary. Existing tests can satisfy
a requirement without adding tests or manufacturing a failure in working code.

For each additional case, identify the plausible regression it would catch that
the existing cases would miss. Expand combinations when they exercise different
decisions or meaningful interactions. Equivalent inputs usually need representative
cases rather than every permutation. Preserve explicitly required scenarios and
regressions from demonstrated bugs; test counts and coverage percentages alone do
not establish redundancy.

Choose the least expensive approved public seam that can detect the actual
failure, preserving behavior rather than internal structure. If the agreed seam
makes necessary coverage impractical, surface the design tradeoff through the
project's design workflow. A new seam requires the existing approval process;
internal mocks are not a shortcut around it. Then use TDD for the missing behavior.

## Verification and evidence

Choose focused checks from the changed behavior and its callers, shared fixtures,
configuration, and dependencies. Broaden selection when impact is uncertain. Run
the repository's required completion checks, including any required full-suite gate.
Rerun checks when a failure, a relevant change, or a remaining uncertainty
invalidates their evidence. Required exact-revision verification always takes
precedence over reusing earlier results.

Plan evidence collection before verification. Retain the required run's command,
exit result, tested source/test identity, logs, and necessary artifacts so the
same run supports completion bookkeeping. If required evidence is missing, collect
it with a scoped additional check and explain the gap. Saving a second report
does not by itself justify replaying the entire scenario matrix. Refer to earlier
results with their actual provenance; do not relabel them as tests of a new revision.

## Suite audits

Audit the wider suite when requested or when measured runtime, flakiness, or
maintenance friction warrants it. Ordinary feature work needs only the local
coverage assessment above. Scope an audit to the affected area or observed cost.

Use existing timing/failure records first; collect missing timings during the
next required run where possible. Group tests by behavior and failure mode,
including parameterized cases, and examine repeated setup and expensive processes.
For a proposed deletion or consolidation, identify the surviving test and explain
which regression protections it retains. Verify the affected behavior and required
completion checks after changing tests. Share fixture builders where useful while
preserving scenario isolation. Keep uncertain coverage until it can be evaluated.

## Existing implementation reviews

Give the existing reviewers the coverage map, actual check evidence, and repository
testing policy. Spec review checks required behavior and regressions. Standards
review considers redundant coverage, unnecessary scenario combinations, costly
setup, fixture ownership, isolation, and brittle assertions. A blocker needs a
concrete correctness, reliability, or maintenance consequence; a preference alone
remains optional. This adds review guidance, not another reviewer or completion gate.

name: codebase-design
description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
---

# Codebase Design

Design **deep modules**: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface, placed at a clean seam, testable through that interface. Use this language and these principles wherever code is being designed or restructured. The aim is leverage for callers, locality for maintainers, and testability for everyone.

## Glossary

Use these terms exactly: don't substitute "component," "service," "API," or "boundary." Consistent language is the whole point.

**Module**: anything with an interface and an implementation. Deliberately scale-agnostic: a function, class, package, or tier-spanning slice. _Avoid_: unit, component, service.

**Interface**: everything a caller must know to use the module correctly: the type signature, but also invariants, ordering constraints, error modes, required configuration, and performance characteristics. _Avoid_: API, signature (too narrow, they refer only to the type-level surface).

**Implementation**: what's inside a module, its body of code. Distinct from **Adapter**: a thing can be a small adapter with a large implementation (a Postgres repo) or a large adapter with a small implementation (an in-memory fake). Reach for "adapter" when the seam is the topic; "implementation" otherwise.

**Depth**: leverage at the interface. The amount of behaviour a caller (or test) can exercise per unit of interface they have to learn. A module is **deep** when a large amount of behaviour sits behind a small interface, **shallow** when the interface is nearly as complex as the implementation.

**Seam** _(Michael Feathers)_: a place where you can alter behaviour without editing in that place; the *location* at which a module's interface lives. Where to put the seam is its own design decision, distinct from what goes behind it. _Avoid_: boundary (overloaded with DDD's bounded context).

**Adapter**: a concrete thing that satisfies an interface at a seam. Describes *role* (what slot it fills), not substance (what's inside).

**Leverage**: what callers get from depth. More capability per unit of interface they learn. One implementation pays back across N call sites and M tests.

**Locality**: what maintainers get from depth. Change, bugs, knowledge, and verification concentrate in one place rather than spreading across callers. Fix once, fixed everywhere.

## Deep vs shallow

**Deep module** = small interface + lots of implementation:

```
┌─────────────────────┐
│   Small Interface   │  ← Few methods, simple params
├─────────────────────┤
│                     │
│  Deep Implementation│  ← Complex logic hidden
│                     │
└─────────────────────┘
```

**Shallow module** = large interface + little implementation (avoid):

```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│       Large Interface           │  ← Many methods, complex params
├─────────────────────────────────┤
│  Thin Implementation            │  ← Just passes through
└─────────────────────────────────┘
```

When designing an interface, ask:

- Can I reduce the number of methods?
- Can I simplify the parameters?
- Can I hide more complexity inside?

## Principles

- **Depth is a property of the interface, not the implementation.** A deep module can be internally composed of small, mockable, swappable parts; they just aren't part of the interface. A module can have **internal seams** (private to its implementation, used by its own tests) as well as the **external seam** at its interface.
- **The deletion test.** Imagine deleting the module. If complexity vanishes, it was a pass-through. If complexity reappears across N callers, it was earning its keep.
- **The interface is the test surface.** Callers and tests cross the same seam. If you want to test *past* the interface, the module is probably the wrong shape.
- **One adapter means a hypothetical seam. Two adapters means a real one.** Don't introduce a seam unless something actually varies across it.

## Designing for testability

Good interfaces make testing natural:

1. **Accept dependencies, don't create them.**

   ```typescript
   // Testable
   function processOrder(order, paymentGateway) {}

   // Hard to test
   function processOrder(order) {
     const gateway = new StripeGateway();
   }
   ```

2. **Return results, don't produce side effects.**

   ```typescript
   // Testable
   function calculateDiscount(cart): Discount {}

   // Hard to test
   function applyDiscount(cart): void {
     cart.total -= discount;
   }
   ```

3. **Small surface area.** Fewer methods = fewer tests needed. Fewer params = simpler test setup.

## Relationships

- A **Module** has exactly one **Interface** (the surface it presents to callers and tests).
- **Depth** is a property of a **Module**, measured against its **Interface**.
- A **Seam** is where a **Module**'s **Interface** lives.
- An **Adapter** sits at a **Seam** and satisfies the **Interface**.
- **Depth** produces **Leverage** for callers and **Locality** for maintainers.

## Rejected framings

- **Depth as ratio of implementation-lines to interface-lines** (Ousterhout): rewards padding the implementation. We use depth-as-leverage instead.
- **"Interface" as the TypeScript `interface` keyword or a class's public methods**: too narrow: interface here includes every fact a caller must know.
- **"Boundary"**: overloaded with DDD's bounded context. Say **seam** or **interface**.

## Going deeper

- **Deepening a cluster given its dependencies**, see [DEEPENING.md](DEEPENING.md): dependency categories, seam discipline, and replace-don't-layer testing.
- **Exploring alternative interfaces**, see [DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md](DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md): spin up parallel sub-agents to design the interface several radically different ways, then compare on depth, locality, and seam placement.
